name: Molecular sieve and glycol dehydration
applications: LNG and NGL cryogenic plants (molecular sieve)
principle: Water is removed so it cannot form hydrates, ice or corrosive liquids. Glycol units absorb water into triethylene glycol, which is regenerated by heating, and are enough for pipeline specifications. Cryogenic plants use molecular sieve beds that adsorb water to very low levels and are regenerated by hot gas in a timed cycle. NETL's LNG model dries gas to below 0.5 ppmv water ahead of liquefaction.

performance.metric: water content after molecular sieve dehydration for LNG

source.note: NETL, Life Cycle GHG Perspective on Exporting LNG from the United States: 2019 Update, DOE/NETL-2019/2041, 12 September 2019, Exhibits 5-7 and 5-11, Appendix B

advantages: Glycol units are low cost for pipeline gas
limitations: Glycol regeneration vents BTEX and methane unless controlled
Molecular sieves need regeneration heat and periodic replacement
Adsorbent dusting can foul downstream exchangers
